title: PISA: Efficient Precision-Slice Framework for LLMs with Adaptive Numerical Type
problem: LLM quantization is ineffective due to outliers; mixed-precision approaches suffer from value-wise granularity and complex encoding/decoding hardware.
motivation: On-device LLM deployment requires extreme efficiency; outliers in weight distributions prevent aggressive quantization.
method: PISA splits each 16-bit value into a 4-bit portion and a 12-bit portion, exploiting the fact that higher-order bits are often sparse (mostly zeros). An 'early bird' mechanism looks at just the 4-bit portion to predict whether the final result will matter, letting the system skip expensive calculations when they won't affect the answer. This integrates with systolic arrays, the hardware grids that accelerate matrix math in AI accelerators.
key_novelty: The innovation is splitting 16-bit values into 4-bit and 12-bit slices, then using the 4-bit portion to predict result importance and skip unnecessary computation.
contributions: Precision-slice 16-bit to 4-bit/12-bit splitting exploiting higher-order bit sparsity
Early bird mechanism predicting computation importance from 4-bit results for efficient skipping
Integration with existing accelerators (systolic arrays) without complex encoding/decoding
1.3-4.3x performance boost, 14.3-66.7% energy efficiency improvement, minimal accuracy loss
limitations: Evaluation on specific LLM architectures; cross-model generalization not discussed.
primary_theme: Precision-slice quantization with early bird prediction for efficient LLM inference
